topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames complement as an important but terminology-heavy subject and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Complement cascade fundamentals and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how to understand the complement cascade, whose central C3 cleavage step connects activation to immune effects.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition generates enough surface-bound C3b to overcome clearance and trigger complement activity.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement translates into immune actions that promote pathogen elimination.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects the functions of individual complement components to the distinct clinical consequences of their deficiency.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains pathogen adaptations that undermine complement, including an antibody-binding adaptation exploited in medicine and research.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and announces adaptive immunity as the next subject.
